profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.tagline: BAG FULL OF LOUD NOISE AND MISSING PARTS
profiles.profile: This is the kind of golf that keeps asking for a miracle and then immediately snaps the putter in half. The ball-striking and the short game both take turns face-planting, and the putter has been actively filing complaints too. He can flash a little tee-to-green life, but it never sticks because some other part of the bag decides to commit arson. The recurring theme is ugly but simple: there’s usually one competent piece in the truck while the rest of the round is busy dragging it into a ditch.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.tagline: APPROACH CHEAT CODE, PUTTER ON MUTE
profiles.profile: When the irons show up, this guy can look like a problem. The approach play is the engine here, and when it’s cooking, the whole round gets a little dangerous for the rest of the room. The catch is the driver and putter keep acting like they were hired from two different companies and don’t know each other. It’s a very usable profile with some teeth, but also a classic reminder that one hot club does not mean the rest of the bag has stopped being weird.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.tagline: FOUND THE CUP ONCE, THEN SET THE HOUSE ON FIRE
profiles.profile: This profile lives in that fun little zone where the results can look respectable while the golf underneath is still trying to eat the furniture. The wins are real, but so is the constant bleed from tee to green, especially when the driver and short game go wandering off together like idiots. He’s had a couple of windows where the scoring hung around anyway, which tells you there’s some grit here, but the overall file is volatile as hell. When it’s bad, it’s not one leak — it’s the whole basement taking water.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.tagline: IRON PLAY IN THE TRUNK, DRIVER IN WITNESS PROTECTION
profiles.profile: This is a weird bag that keeps teasing competence and then immediately drilling a crater with the irons. The tee game can pop, the short game can help, and every once in a while the round looks almost sane. Then the approach play shows up with a clown suit on and reminds everybody that golf is a stupid sport. The shape here is basically: enough tools to avoid being hopeless, not enough consistency to stop the mid-round nonsense from taking over.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: ALL GAS, THEN A RANDOM BODY SHOP VISIT
profiles.profile: This dude can absolutely post a round that looks like he stole somebody else’s swing, which is why the file is annoying in the first place. There’s real pop off the tee, and the better stretches show he can stack tee-to-green and putting into something dangerous. But the approach and short game keep taking little ransom notes from the scorecard, and that’s where the nonsense starts. It’s a volatile bag with enough upside to be spicy, but enough self-sabotage that it never gets to just be smooth about it.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: The first look says this is a mess of a tee-to-green day with just enough putting to keep the body from being identified. The irons and short game both leaked hard, and that’s the kind of combo that turns a round into a recovery mission nobody asked for. The putter was the only club acting like it had read the memo. Hard to call it anything bigger than one ugly snapshot, but the snapshot is pretty clear: the scoring clubs did not get the save-the-day call.
